Net combined hybrid system output for front-wheel-drive models ('194 net hp on Front-Wheel Drive (FWD) equipped models'); Toyota quotes 196 net hp with e-AWD. Automotive Fleet and Edmunds (194 hp @ 6,000 rpm for the LE) agree. KBB and CarsDirect list 150 hp, the gasoline engine alone (see conflicts). KBB's 2024 Prius specs list '150 @ 6000 RPM' (the gasoline engine alone). The Toyota Dynamic Force engine article gives the M20A-FXS '112 kW (150 hp; 152 PS) at 6,000 rpm', and Edmunds lists '194 hp @ 6,000 rpm' for the LE. CAVEAT: 6,000 rpm is the engine's peak-power speed; the 194 hp system figure has no separate rpm, since the motor-generators add power independent of engine speed. No Toyota figure was surfaced. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

CAVEAT: not a combined system torque and not the engine torque. Toyota's 2024 release headline reads 'Powerful Hybrid System with up to 196-hp and 152 lb.-ft. of torque' without saying which component it describes; AutoInformed attributes 152 lb-ft to the front-drive motor-generator. The gasoline engine alone is 139 lb-ft (188 Nm) per Cars.com, KBB and the WA State DES database (see conflicts). Toyota publishes no system torque in the results found. Carried over from the earlier trading-card research record (engine/data/research/seed-2026-11-10.json). Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

fields.note: UNOFFICIAL. A PriusChat member's notes on the fifth-generation transaxles list the 2.0 HEV final drive as 77:21 (3.667), the 1.8 HEV as 74:20 (3.700) and the PHEV as 78:20 (3.900), with the 2.0 HEV MG2 reduction 53:16 (3.313).
